Dear Dr Simon Anderson
RE: Mr. Daniel McCrae, DOB:17 October 1962

I am writing this letter to refer you Mr. McCrea, a 52-year -old barrister, who is presenting with symptoms   Commented [jc1]: spelling
and signs suggestive of adenocarcinoma of the colon. Your further management would be highly
appreciated.

Mr. McCrea is married and has four offspring's. Regarding his social and family history, he is a smoker and   Commented [jc2]: spelling
has no family history of colorectal cancer, colonic polyps or inflammatory bowel disease.
                                                                                                              Commented [jc3]: children

On 19/9/13, he presented complaining of fever, sore throat, headache and body itching. He was diagnosed
with a viral infection and was giving paracetamol. Six months later, he came back complaining of tiredness,   Commented [jc4]: given
fatigue, gases and abdominal discomfort. Upon physical examination, abdomen was soft, lax with no             Commented [jc5]: his
masses, guarding or rebound and normal bowel sound. Moreover, he was ordered CBC, FOBT and                    Commented [jc6]: and
colonoscopy to be revealed two weeks later.

On today's review, he still feels unwell. His result came out revealing that his CBC and FOBT are both
normal. However, his colonoscopy showed malignancy in the ascending colon; biopsy was taken and
adenocarcinoma was diagnosed.

In light of the above, your further assessment and management are required promptly. For any queries,
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Your sincerely,

Doctor
